citation: Johnson L, Wilcox S, Mankoff J, Stricker RB (2014). Severity of chronic Lyme disease compared to other chronic conditions: a quality of life survey. PeerJ 2:e322.
verification: Uploaded full PDF text reviewed; specific tables and narrative distinguished.
scope: Selected online respondents reporting persistent symptoms >6 months after antibiotic treatment; diagnoses and outcomes self-reported, not independently confirmed. Not representative county incident Lyme cases.

findings.source: PDF page 7, Table 4, full working sample column
findings.note: Narrative page 12 says approximately 42%; retain table and narrative distinction.
Narrative page 12 gives 25%; do not silently reconcile.

findings.measure: At least $5,000 annual Lyme-related out-of-pocket expenses
findings.note: Narrative page 11 approximately 43%; discussion gives 46%. Table 4 is used for this extraction.

findings.measure: Reported receiving disability as a result of CLD
findings.note: Self-reported; does not establish adjudicated SSA eligibility or disability risk among all Lyme cases.

limitations: Self-selected online sample enriched for persistent illness
Cannot estimate the probability of chronic disability among newly diagnosed county cases
Does not quantify total societal costs; annual spending bands are not means
Some table/narrative values differ; do not combine them as consistent estimates
